repository.access: authorized selected source packet; not a runnable checkout

decision.binary_candidate: Arrow IPC stream; internal compression none; negotiated HTTP gzip
decision.simpler_baseline_and_fallback: Lossless schema-described row JSON plus gzip
decision.current_resident_layout: Existing row-object provider and Crossfilter for first proof
decision.hosting_scope: Dedicated instance per paying customer; instance-scoped data/cache/resources; platform choice owned by fourth hosting track

adoption_gates.classification: proposed shaping thresholds; no measured benchmark results
adoption_gates.mandatory_correctness: Exact supported values/types/keys, row meaning, scope, coverage, completion and lifecycle; explicit unsupported states
adoption_gates.primary_proxy: 100k complete scatter rows with x/y, 32 text color labels and durable text keys; 10k and numeric-color controls

latency.metric: p95 source/request-to-completed-filter-ready-view, including server/decoder startup, row bridge and current consumers

memory_alternative.metric: Peak incremental attributable client data across JS heap, unique backing buffers, workers and known native/WASM/plot allocations, including old/new overlap

adoption_gates.benefit_rule: Pass latency OR memory alternative; all mandatory correctness/capacity and applicable regression guards still apply
adoption_gates.responsiveness_diagnostic: Investigate newly introduced main-thread tasks over 50 ms in the 10k case; worker/cooperative techniques conditional on evidence

runs.note: Coarse p95; record raw samples/uncertainty, separate cold and warm caches, extend only for a threshold-crossing uncertainty or concrete risk

provisional_capacity_policy.enforcement: Known bounded server response; incremental reader counts application-visible decoded bytes. Whole-body JSON charges actual parse/assembly cost and needs no custom record parser. Native decoder/network queues remain measured uncertainty, not a guaranteed hard cap.
provisional_capacity_policy.oversize_behavior: Narrower complete projection, exact aggregate with truthful trace, or explicit partial/unsupported result; never silent first-N truncation
provisional_capacity_policy.cache_scope: Authenticated instance + authoritative snapshot + query/population + row grain/order/keys + schema/projection/dictionary; no cross-instance customer result cache

first_proof: Paired row JSON/Arrow 10k and 100k current-host-row proof with compatible field settings
Broaden only if evidence can reverse the decision
Bounded read-only adapter fixture including database/driver/server costs
checks_not_run: pnpm --filter exploreda exec vitest run src/test/lib/analysis/evaluateProject.test.ts src/test/lib/analysis/useAnalysisEvaluation.test.tsx src/test/lib/analysis/sourceRowIdentity.test.ts src/hooks/CrossfilterWrapper.test.ts

recommendations.proposal: Require authoritative snapshot, schema, row meaning, coverage and completion metadata before optimizing bytes.
recommendations.rationale: Existing evaluation revision/counts do not prove a remote source snapshot or completed coverage. Keys, field types and filter scope determine whether parts can be assembled safely.

repository_evidence.observation: No remote snapshot, batch or truncation contract.
Realm-local array revision and final-row counts are not server snapshot/exhaustion evidence.
Linked, local and other-filter populations differ.

confidence.basis: Correctness requirement directly supported by source; final contract belongs to query track.

proof.test: F0/F8: typed keys, changed snapshot/schema/order/dictionary, duplicate/gap/truncated/empty results and mismatched scope. Use independent application counters and tested end/error handling.
proof.pass: No invalid/partial result commits as complete; unknown counts and logical exhaustion remain explicit.
proof.reversal: Fields/IDs may be consolidated into a smaller canonical descriptor if it preserves all invariants.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: One bounded schema-described JSON result with the same logical metadata.
recommendations.principal_cost: Small validator and descriptor; do not invent a general query/cache framework.

recommendations.proposal: Investigate internally uncompressed Arrow IPC streams with negotiated HTTP gzip as the default binary candidate.
recommendations.rationale: Standard typed batches may reduce parsing/transfer cost, but current row reconstruction and provider cost can consume the savings. No performance win is measured.

repository_evidence.observation: Current project bridge constructs rows and has no external-evaluation prop.
Current provider uses rows and object field maps.

confidence.basis: Feasible standard candidate; end-to-end advantage remains untested.

proof.test: First paired 10k/100k scatter proof with real keys, identical schema/field settings/commit timing, cold assets and server cost.
proof.pass: Mandatory correctness plus latency or memory gate, with applicable regression/capacity guards.
proof.reversal: Retain JSON if gates fail; prefer column JSON if it wins with lower integration cost.

recommendations.principal_cost: Arrow dependency/startup, schema mapping, validation, possible buffer assembly and row materialization.

recommendations.proposal: Keep lossless schema-described row JSON as the baseline and fallback.
recommendations.rationale: It reaches current row consumers directly and avoids a new column engine. Plain JSON.stringify needs explicit handling for existing exceptional raw values.

repository_evidence.observation: Existing raw scalar domain includes undefined.
Existing file format handles undefined/nonfinite values but is not a remote protocol.
Rows remain the consumer boundary.

confidence.basis: Lowest-change baseline; exact restoration and consumer behavior still need proof.

proof.test: Golden raw-value corpus, including absent/undefined/null, nonfinite/signed zero, typed keys and numeric-looking text. Count whole-body parsing temporaries.
proof.pass: Supported values and effective behavior match; unsafe semantics are rejected.
proof.reversal: Select a proven encoding that clears the same gates; JSON cannot waive unsupported consumer capabilities.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: Column JSON with a direct ordinary-array-to-row transpose.
recommendations.principal_cost: Text parsing and resident rows; explicit schema/exceptions; a bounded collector adds cost if client byte enforcement requires it.

recommendations.proposal: Decode and validate outside the provider, materialize rows once, and publish each completed snapshot once.
recommendations.rationale: New data references can rebuild provider state and restore settings. Streaming arrival alone does not make current full-snapshot filters exact.

repository_evidence.observation: Data replacement rebuilds runtime structures; saved settings can trigger restore.
Schema is not automatically applied without compatible settings; project tracing has a separate boundary.
Previous completed same-query result can overlap incoming work.

confidence.basis: Directly observed rebuild and row interface; allocation totals unmeasured.

proof.test: Instrument decode, materialization, setup count, restore, old/new overlap and exact chart interactions.
proof.pass: One complete publication; obsolete or invalid work never commits; same field settings and row meaning for both formats.
proof.reversal: Progressive publication requires a separately justified consumer seam and truthful partial-view semantics.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: Native lossless row JSON parsed once into the same boundary.
recommendations.principal_cost: Temporary column/row overlap; current provider and project row copies remain chargeable.

recommendations.proposal: Use one compression layer by default; compare gzip, moderate Brotli and identity with recorded settings.
recommendations.rationale: HTTP decoding differs from IPC/Parquet internal codecs. Extra CPU/startup must be justified by elapsed-time savings and per-instance resources.

repository_evidence.observation: No direct Arrow/Parquet codec in the supplied manifest.
Wire savings do not remove consumer setup cost.

confidence.basis: Mechanisms verified; winning settings are workload-dependent.

proof.test: Record encoded/decoded bytes, encode/decode CPU and complete-view time on fast, 100 Mbps and 10 Mbps conditions.
proof.pass: Compression improves the full path without exceeding instance budgets; tiny responses avoid unjustified overhead.
proof.reversal: Use identity for small bodies or a different measured level/codec when elapsed time wins.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: Identity encoding for small results; gzip for the first bounded comparison.
recommendations.principal_cost: Compressor/decompressor state and CPU; higher levels and extra registered codecs may increase startup.

recommendations.proposal: Separate lossless transport support from supported consumer semantics; reject silent coercion.
recommendations.rationale: The scalar/type model lacks explicit bigint, decimal precision, fine temporal units, binary and nested semantics. Current parsing can reinterpret numeric-looking text.

repository_evidence.observation: No exact rich-type analytical capability is declared.
Numeric-string parsing and millisecond temporal behavior need explicit guards.
Scalar type changes affect key and filter meaning.

confidence.basis: Source and specifications establish the risk; supported subset remains a proof decision.

proof.test: F0 exactness corpus from driver through raw and effective browser values, including overflow, decimal scale, zone/unit, leading BOM and mixed/nested states.
proof.pass: Preserve values/meaning or return an explicit unsupported diagnostic before lossy conversion.
proof.reversal: A richer type can be enabled only after its consumer operations and parity are proven.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: Lossless JSON or intentional typed-text display/key use where current semantics are safe.
recommendations.principal_cost: Schema/type mapping, validation and explicit capability errors.

recommendations.proposal: Measure dictionary/null/integer encodings; preserve float64 unless an exact narrower source type is established.
recommendations.rationale: Repeated categories can be compact; unique text and sparse values can reverse the advantage. Builder state, string decoding and HTTP compression affect the result.

repository_evidence.observation: Raw value distinctions must survive packing.
Rounding can change exact selection and coordinate values.

confidence.basis: Analytical size advantages exist; compression/timing gains are unmeasured.

proof.test: F2/F4/F5/F6 with cardinality, null fraction and runs varied independently; round-trip width/precision boundaries.
proof.pass: Measured net benefit with fixed validated dictionary meaning and exact values.
proof.reversal: Use flat strings/simple widths when encoding overhead loses; invisible quantization is rejected.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: Straightforward lossless primitive columns or JSON plus HTTP compression.
recommendations.principal_cost: Dictionary hash tables/mappings, null state, width scans and decode work.

recommendations.proposal: Admit snapshots using separate row, wire, decoded, retained and peak budgets.
recommendations.rationale: Rows, field maps, Crossfilter, provenance and charts can exceed transport buffers. Full snapshots remain valid when actual total cost fits.

repository_evidence.observation: Multiple retained structures are visible; helper internals are omitted.
Chart work and large-N sensitivity remain after transfer.
Trace/evaluation retention may scale with inputs.

confidence.level: high for policy; low for initial numeric defaults
confidence.basis: Need is source-backed; 64/128/256 MiB values are lab knobs awaiting calibration.

proof.test: Width/text/provenance plus replacement, cancellation and oversize cases; unique-allocation ledger across workers and known native data.
proof.pass: No silent truncation, no off-heap accounting illusion, budgets respected with uncertainty disclosed.
proof.reversal: Change row/byte targets using measured target-hardware results; never infer safety from compressed size alone.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: Narrower complete projection or exact server aggregate with truthful coverage/trace.
recommendations.principal_cost: Admission estimation, explicit limits and retained/peak instrumentation.

recommendations.proposal: Use staged end-to-end adoption gates with a predeclared workload and small-output/interaction guards.
recommendations.rationale: The selected packet supplies no executed codec or application measurements. A byte-only benchmark could reward a slower full user path.

repository_evidence.observation: Historical development checks are not current transport evidence.
Proof should preserve meaningful interaction and record identity.

confidence.basis: Transparent falsifiable rule; thresholds are not product SLOs.

proof.test: F0 then paired F1/F2 complete-view runs, project-source variant and actual bounded adapter path; broaden only when evidence could change the decision.
proof.pass: Correctness plus >=20% and >=100 ms p95 benefit, or >=25% attributable peak-memory reduction with <=5% latency regression; apply all guards.
proof.reversal: Retain JSON or select column JSON if Arrow fails; stop transport work if provider/trace dominates.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: Ship the simpler encoding after correctness without adding an unproven binary dependency.
recommendations.principal_cost: Controlled runs, raw samples and instrumentation; avoid a full codec/workload cross product.

recommendations.proposal: Scope caches to instance and immutable snapshot/row domain; defer a general progressive cache.
recommendations.rationale: Equal row counts or local revisions do not establish that new columns describe the same records. Full-row projection coverage differs from partial-row coverage.

repository_evidence.observation: Source version and row grain differ from positional or local tokens.
Chart IDs are evaluation-local.
Subset coverage cannot answer every local scope or filter removal.

confidence.basis: Correctness requirement; expansion capability is optional.

proof.test: Late columns with old/new snapshots, reordered/duplicate keys, expired leases and changed dictionaries.
proof.pass: Only compatible complete row domains merge; otherwise rebuild or refuse extension.
proof.reversal: Enable broader caching only after a measured demand and coherent snapshot capability exist.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: One completed snapshot plus one incoming replacement; refetch coherently on expiry.
recommendations.principal_cost: Pinned key/schema/dictionary metadata, bounded retention and invalidation.

recommendations.proposal: Defer Parquet as the default dynamic query response.
recommendations.rationale: Footer/range/page decoding and reader startup may be unnecessary for bounded dynamic results. Existing immutable Parquet and repeated projections can justify it.

repository_evidence.observation: Rows still required after Parquet decoding.
No selected Parquet decoder in supplied direct dependencies.

confidence.basis: Cost/fit inference; no measured reader comparison.

proof.test: Compare pure-JS and WASM candidates on immutable range-aware files, including footer/extra requests, codecs, startup, copies and row bridge.
proof.pass: Selective-read reuse wins the same full-path gates with exact types.
proof.reversal: Reopen if the adapter/source already stores suitable Parquet or wide projection reuse dominates.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: Arrow stream or lossless JSON for one complete bounded response.
recommendations.principal_cost: Reader/codec dependency, footer/range machinery and optional WASM/IPC bridge; no outer compression for original-byte ranges.

recommendations.proposal: Defer a custom typed-array codec until standard-decoder overhead is a measured blocker.
recommendations.rationale: A small envelope may reduce startup but moves type validation, framing, strings, nulls, dictionary rules and maintenance into the project.

repository_evidence.observation: Current scalar/result semantics already need deliberate mapping.
A custom codec must preserve existing value distinctions.

confidence.basis: Maintenance tradeoff; no custom decoder size/performance evidence.

proof.test: Only after Arrow startup is isolated, compare a restricted scalar prototype with the same validation, row bridge and gates.
proof.pass: Meaningful full-path benefit exceeds owned-format maintenance cost.
proof.reversal: Keep standard Arrow or simpler JSON if savings disappear after complete accounting.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: Standard Arrow IPC, or column JSON if that meets the need.
recommendations.principal_cost: Owned protocol/codec and long-term correctness responsibility; logical metadata remains required for every option.

recommendations.proposal: Keep all customer data/caches within dedicated customer instances and hand platform choice to hosting.
recommendations.rationale: Latest user scope interprets one-server simplicity per paying customer, with automated setup/operation. Transport imposes resource and consistency needs, not a platform selection.

repository_evidence.observation: Existing pnpm/React project remains the application context.
Remote cancellation and instance resource control are additional interface obligations.

confidence.basis: Explicit user constraint; hosting capabilities/costs are not measured here.

proof.test: Hosting validates per-instance routing, secret/data/cache scope, memory/duration/concurrency, cancellation, cleanup, telemetry and automated lifecycle.
proof.pass: A chosen platform meets bounded-response needs; streaming/ranges/shared-memory features are conditional and separately verified.
proof.reversal: No platform choice to reverse in this track; adapt retention/streaming strategy to measured hosting limits.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: Bounded buffered complete responses when streaming is unavailable but budgets fit.
recommendations.principal_cost: Per-instance buffers/snapshot lifecycle and observability; no shared customer result cache or mandatory new durable platform.

recommendations.proposal: Defer a resident column store or Crossfilter rewrite.
recommendations.rationale: Current column getters are object maps over rows; replacing transport does not replace profiles, calculations, filtering, inspection and restore.

repository_evidence.observation: Field maps and restore depend on current row representation.
Scope behavior must survive any consumer change.
A broad provider/renderer rewrite is not a prerequisite to a visible proof.

confidence.basis: Broad current-consumer obligations are visible; a narrow wire experiment is available.

proof.test: First measure provider/index/trace/plot fractions across encodings. Reopen with one narrowly scoped column consumer only if these dominate.
proof.pass: Separate proof preserves exact filtering, raw inspection, calculation, aggregate and restore semantics.
proof.reversal: Only measured consumer dominance and a useful small seam justify shaping this work.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: Current rows, one materialization/commit and release of transient columns.
recommendations.principal_cost: Potentially broad application design and parity work, outside this assignment.

recommendations.proposal: Investigate compact aggregate JSON with truthful same-snapshot trace capability.
recommendations.rationale: Small group counts do not imply a small whole AnalysisEvaluation; earlier stages and per-measure contributor entries can dominate.

repository_evidence.observation: Whole evaluation retains input-scaled structures.
Contributor records are distinct from output values.
Remote compact results cannot silently impersonate full local lineage.

confidence.basis: Repository trace cost visible; future compact trace contract is unresolved.

proof.test: F7: 32-group body versus full current evaluation; source membership/numeric contributors and same-snapshot record inspection.
proof.pass: Latency/startup benefit with honest capabilities, counts and trace meaning.
proof.reversal: Keep required trace data or report capability limitation if coherent deferred inspection is unavailable.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: Complete source snapshot and local evaluation when its cost fits.
recommendations.principal_cost: Additional trace/result seam and snapshot retention if trace is deferred; not selected by transport alone.

recommendations.proposal: Reject end-to-end zero-copy claims for the proposed transport.
recommendations.rationale: Specific typed views/transfers can avoid individual copies, while database conversion, HTTP, strings, row reconstruction, current workers and charts still allocate.

repository_evidence.observation: Observed table posts have no transfer list; actual result-side posting is omitted.
Final rows are copied into chart objects.
Row/index/map construction persists.

confidence.basis: Source and ownership APIs directly contradict a blanket claim.

proof.test: Per-boundary unique-allocation/lifetime ledger plus explicit concat/copy/clone/transfer and row-materialization instrumentation.
proof.pass: Only locally evidenced copy-avoidance claims; disclose unknown native/parser/renderer work.
proof.reversal: A narrower claim may be supported for a proven boundary; no unmeasured whole-system claim.

recommendations.strongest_alternative: Describe the path as typed column transport with measured row materialization and copy costs.
recommendations.principal_cost: Accounting effort; aliases and off-heap buffers must not be double-counted or omitted.
